A breeding population that small triggers what geneticists call a bottleneck event, where inbreeding becomes statistically unavoidable. When fewer than 50 breeding individuals exist, the risk of inherited defects and immune vulnerability increases sharply. Unlike island species that evolved in isolation, the Amur leopard historically ranged across thousands of square kilometers, making such contraction ecologically catastrophic. Habitat fragmentation from logging, road construction, and poaching compressed the species into a narrow corridor along the Russian-Chinese border. By modern conservation standards, this was a red-alert scenario typically associated with species on the brink of functional extinction.
